hints: Use the power law to write $2\log_3(x-1)$ as a single logarithm.
Replace $1$ by $\log_3 3$, then combine the logarithms on the right-hand side.
Equate the positive arguments to obtain $2x+1=3(x-1)^2$.
Expand and collect all terms on one side to display the required three-term quadratic equation.
walkthrough:
Apply the power law of logarithms $k\log_b u = \log_b(u^k)$ to the second term on the right:
$$2\log_3(x - 1) = \log_3\!\left((x - 1)^2\right)$$

Express the constant $1$ in base-$3$ logarithmic form using $1 = \log_3 3$:
$$\log_3(2x + 1) = \log_3 3 + \log_3\!\left((x - 1)^2\right)$$

Use the product rule of logarithms $\log_b A + \log_b B = \log_b(AB)$ to combine the right-hand side:
$$\log_3(2x + 1) = \log_3\!\left(3(x - 1)^2\right)$$

Equate the arguments of the logarithms on both sides:
$$2x + 1 = 3(x - 1)^2$$

Rearrange all terms to one side to form the quadratic equation:
$$3x^2 - 6x - 2x + 3 - 1 = 0$$
$$3x^2 - 8x + 2 = 0$$

hints: Relate this equation to part (a) by setting $x=2y$, since $2x+1=4y+1$ and $x-1=2y-1$.
Substitute $x=2y$ into the quadratic from part (a) and solve the resulting quadratic in $y$.
The logarithm $\log_3(2y-1)$ requires $2y-1>0$; reject any quadratic root that violates this domain.
Round the remaining value to 2 decimal places only after the domain check.
walkthrough: Notice that the equation $\log_3(4y + 1) = 1 + 2\log_3(2y - 1)$ corresponds to the equation in part (a) under the substitution $x = 2y$, since $2(2y) + 1 = 4y + 1$ and $2y - 1 = x - 1$.

Substitute $x = 2y$ into the quadratic equation $3x^2 - 8x + 2 = 0$ obtained in part (a):
$$3(2y)^2 - 8(2y) + 2 = 0$$
$$3(4y^2) - 16y + 2 = 0$$
$$12y^2 - 16y + 2 = 0$$

Divide by $2$ to simplify the coefficients:
$$6y^2 - 8y + 1 = 0$$

Apply the quadratic formula with $a = 6$, $b = -8$, and $c = 1$:
$$y = \dfrac{-(-8) \pm \sqrt{(-8)^2 - 4(6)(1)}}{2(6)} = \dfrac{8 \pm \sqrt{64 - 24}}{12} = \dfrac{8 \pm \sqrt{40}}{12} = \dfrac{4 \pm \sqrt{10}}{6}$$

Evaluate the two potential solutions numerically using $\sqrt{10} \approx 3.16228$:
$$y_1 = \dfrac{4 + 3.16228}{6} = \dfrac{7.16228}{6} \approx 1.1937$$
$$y_2 = \dfrac{4 - 3.16228}{6} = \dfrac{0.83772}{6} \approx 0.1396$$

Examine the domain restrictions for the logarithms in the original equation:
The term $\log_3(2y - 1)$ requires $2y - 1 > 0 \implies y > \dfrac{1}{2} = 0.5$.
For $y_2 \approx 0.1396$, we have $2(0.1396) - 1 = -0.7208 < 0$, which is outside the domain of the logarithm, so $y_2$ must be rejected.

Round the valid solution $y_1$ correct to 2 decimal places:
$$y = 1.19$$
